title: Familial hypercholesterolemia: defective binding of lipoproteins to cultured fibroblasts associated with impaired regulation of 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl coenzyme A reductase activity
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
population: Cultured skin fibroblasts from normal subjects and from five unrelated subjects with homozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia
funder: Grants from the American Heart Association (72629), the Dallas Diabetes Association and the National Institutes of Health (HL 16024 and GM 19258); J.L.G. held a USPHS Research Career Development Award (GM 70,227).
result: Normal fibroblasts bound 125I-LDL with high affinity and specificity; at 37 degrees C binding sites were saturated at an LDL concentration of 20 micrograms per ml, with a maximum of about 250,000 molecules bound per cell. High-affinity binding of similar magnitude was absent in cells from five unrelated homozygotes for familial hypercholesterolaemia. The binding appeared to be a required step by which LDL suppresses HMG-CoA reductase, the rate-controlling enzyme of cholesterol synthesis.
